passage.text: In many Nigerian villages, the tradition of communal labour, known locally by various names, remains a powerful example of cooperation. Neighbours gather to help one family build a house, clear a farm, or celebrate a wedding, expecting nothing in return except the knowledge that the favour will be returned when they themselves are in need. In an increasingly individualistic world, such traditions offer a valuable lesson in the power of collective effort.

passage.text: Reading opens the mind to endless possibilities, exposing young people to worlds, ideas and perspectives beyond their immediate environment. Studies consistently show that students who read widely tend to perform better academically, possess larger vocabularies, and demonstrate stronger critical thinking skills. Unfortunately, reading culture among Nigerian youths has declined in recent years, a trend many attribute to the growing dominance of social media and the scarcity of affordable, engaging books. Reviving this culture will require concerted effort from parents, schools and publishers alike, to make reading both accessible and enjoyable once again.
